title: 54 Photos That Take You Back Through 2017 | Year in Review 2017
body:
Happy New Year.

2017 was the second year of QDaily's "Picture of the Day" column, and the second time we have picked our "Photos of the Year." As of today we have published 301 updates and 2,181 images, asking ourselves the same question over and over: is this piece of news — this photograph — truly "important" enough to belong here?

The column works like this. We license images from photo agencies, then choose them by two measures: the quality of the picture and the weight of the event. Our first stop is usually the various "today's photos" selections that editors at the big news organizations and picture agencies have already sifted through. In the "And these are also worth a look" section, we tend to share things that made us think, "huh, that's interesting" — and "interesting," as you'll see, doesn't always mean light-hearted.

For all sorts of reasons, a selection like this cannot possibly hold every important event of the year.

Looking back over the past year, division, estrangement, violence, fear, destruction, and displacement turn up again and again. When we ran our year-end photo wrap-up last December, we put the words "finally behind us" in the headline to wave goodbye to a turbulent 2016 — events like Brexit and Donald Trump's election as U.S. president had shown people a world growing ever more fractured. Sadly, 2017 did not get better.

We earlier [reported on Japan's character of the year, "北" (North)](https://www.qdaily.com/articles/48201.html), and readers left 73 nominations in the comments. They cannot stand for everything that happened over the past year — after all, the legalization of same-sex marriage in several countries was genuinely heartening — but the unease and anxiety running through them is plain to see.

As we say each time: we believe no part of the world should rank as categorically more important than another. What matters is seeing more, exploring more. And being ready.

**1. Britain's Prime Minister Lays Out the Brexit Plan**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201712281710447j1krKn4f6NmvFpM.jpg-w600)

London, UK. British Prime Minister Theresa May delivers a speech at Lancaster House, laying out a specific plan for Brexit. It was the first time Britain had offered a clear "Brexit roadmap" since the country voted to leave the EU the previous June. In her remarks she said it was impossible for the UK to stay in the European Single Market, because doing so would mean Britain had not really left the EU at all. She called for a new, equal partnership between the UK and the EU rather than a "half-in, half-out" status as a semi-member or associate member.

**2. Trump Is Sworn In as U.S. President**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227164517y9O6oiQLfqG2vsHS.jpg-w600)

Washington, D.C. The Capitol has been set up and spectators are filing into their seats, waiting for Donald Trump's inauguration. According to a CNN poll released on January 17, Trump's approval rating stood at just 40 percent, the lowest pre-inauguration rating of any incoming U.S. president since 1992. By January 18, more than 60 Democratic members of Congress had announced they would boycott the inauguration, saying they considered Trump's election illegitimate.

**3. Federer's Grand Slam**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228171416DH2KUJLNx6GSvIhT.jpg-w600)

Melbourne, Australia. Roger Federer kisses the trophy at the 2017 Australian Open men's singles awards ceremony. The match was the ninth Grand Slam final between Federer and Rafael Nadal in six years. Federer beat Nadal 6–4, 3–6, 6–1, 3–6, 6–3 to claim his 18th Grand Slam title — and his first in nearly five years.

**4. Bus Barricade**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228171444KNEFtmxXHZ70sckC.jpg-w600)

Dresden, Germany. Syrian artist Manaf Halboun stood three buses on end near a church to draw attention to the suffering of civilians in Aleppo, Syria. Halboun drew on the Syrian civil war, during which civilians stood buses upright in the streets as barricades and shields against snipers.

**5. The Academy Awards**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227164732PAHnUKdLfi20Fu5v.jpg-w600)

Los Angeles, USA. At the 89th Academy Awards, *La La Land* producer Jordan Horowitz, having spotted the error, holds up the correct Best Picture card to signal the audience and invites the cast and crew of *Moonlight* onstage. Presenters had mistakenly carried the Best Actress envelope onstage, [causing a mix-up](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/38214.html) at the ceremony. *Moonlight* went on to win three awards: Best Picture, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Best Supporting Actor.

**6. Flight**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228171646Z36Bb8dIHs2u5FWU.jpg-w600)

Mosul, Iraq. A man clutches his daughter and runs from an area held by ISIS toward a zone controlled by Iraqi special forces. According to figures released by UNHCR in March, about 700,000 people were trapped between the two sides at the time, facing a crisis of food and supply shortages.

**7. 16.7 Meters**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228171704AdXeUrtfzk74S0HP.jpg-w600)

Tokyo, Japan. Yahoo Japan mounted a 31-meter-long advertisement on the outer wall of the Sony Building in Ginza to mark the sixth anniversary of the March 11 Great East Japan Earthquake. Inside the giant text runs a single line set in red on red — and the height of that red lettering is exactly the height of the largest tsunami wave recorded during the quake, at Ofunato in Iwate Prefecture: 16.7 meters.

**8. The London Terror Attack**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228172039nF9QEvRPujwVUkSI.jpg-w600)

London, UK. Police cordon off streets near the Houses of Parliament after the attack. On the afternoon of March 22 local time, a suspected terrorist drove a vehicle onto Westminster Bridge, mowing down several pedestrians, then was shot dead by police as he tried to force his way into the Parliament building. The attack left five people dead, including the suspect, and more than 40 others injured. Prime Minister Theresa May later issued a statement saying the UK's terrorism threat level would stay at "Severe" and would not be raised. The Metropolitan Police confirmed the attacker was Khalid Masood, a 52-year-old British man born in Kent who had earlier been convicted of a string of offenses, including assault and possession of an offensive weapon.

**9. Fearless Girl**

![](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228171826OkUZXb0d5fpRQaiN.jpg-w600)

New York City, USA. Mayor Bill de Blasio announces that *Fearless Girl*, the new statue installed across from the famous Charging Bull on Wall Street, will stay where it is through International Women's Day 2018. [*Fearless Girl*](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/42206.html) is the work of sculptor Kristen Visbal, commissioned as a gift to the women of New York by State Street Global Advisors, one of Wall Street's major financial firms, to call on people to confront the "glass ceiling" women face at work.

**10. North Korean Guard**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228172253NoUODbSIuqmfC8l9.jpg-w600)

Pyongyang, North Korea. As a group of foreign journalists tours a local catfish farm, a photographer captures a female soldier standing guard. Around 200 foreign reporters had been invited by the North Korean government to Pyongyang to cover the "major event" of the 105th anniversary of Kim Il-sung's birth. The press delegation toured important local sights and construction projects along officially designated routes. Journalists were barred from bringing lighters, mobile phones, or computers.

**11. Spacewalk**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228172421jNU307aAuPhkFTvY.jpg-w600)

NASA released a new photograph taken from the International Space Station showing American astronaut Peggy Whitson on a spacewalk. As of April 24, Whitson, 57, had logged 534 days in space, passing fellow NASA astronaut Jeff Williams to become the American astronaut with the most total time in space.

**12. Macron Elected President of France**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227164858Q8GLdA16Wwfa4PIi.jpg-w600)

Paris, France. Emmanuel Macron wins the 2017 French presidential election and, with his wife at his side, waves to cheering supporters at the Louvre. In the second round of voting, the 39-year-old Macron beat Marine Le Pen, candidate of the far-right National Front, by 66.1 percent to 33.9 percent, becoming the youngest president in French history. His wife, Brigitte, is 24 years his senior and was his drama teacher when Macron was in secondary school.

**13. Moon Jae-in Begins His Presidency**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227164956maYc5lrgRX2TODkV.jpg-w600)

Seoul, South Korea. South Korea's newly inaugurated president, Moon Jae-in, speaks by phone with Lee Sun-jin, chairman of the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff, receiving a briefing on North Korean military movements and South Korea's readiness. On May 10 local time, the 64-year-old Moon was formally sworn in as South Korea's 19th president and began work on his first day in office, filling the power vacuum left by the impeachment and removal of former president Park Geun-hye. His policies include talks with North Korea to ease tensions on the peninsula and opposition to the deployment of the U.S. Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) missile system in South Korea.

**14. Bicycle Graveyard**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228172900C0VrDLGqgpdkAjBM.jpg-w600)

Hangzhou. On a patch of empty ground in the city's south, tens of thousands of shared bikes lie abandoned in the open. Spread across more than a thousand square meters, bikes of every brand are piled together in a startling sprawl. By June this year, the number of shared bikes impounded for illegal parking in Hangzhou's main districts had reportedly topped 20,000. Faced with bikes left everywhere, regulators had little choice but to gather them in one place and tell the companies to come deal with them. So far the results have been poor: [most bike companies have yet to respond](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/48331.html) to the question of what to do with the vehicles.

**15. Hong Kong's 20th Handover Anniversary**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227165224MAcIGLje2waoXTbB.jpg-w600)

Hong Kong. Fireworks light up Victoria Harbour to mark the 20th anniversary of the founding of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Shortly before, at a regular press briefing on June 30, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lu Kang said that "the Sino-British Joint Declaration, as a historical document, no longer has any practical significance, and it is not at all binding on the Chinese central government's administration of Hong Kong" — a remark that drew wide debate on social media. Lu was responding to comments made on June 29 by British Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson, who had said, "The rule of law, an independent judiciary, and a free press are key to Hong Kong's success. Hong Kong's future success will undoubtedly rest on the rights and freedoms the Sino-British Joint Declaration grants Hong Kong." That same day, a U.S. State Department spokesperson also said the United States was "concerned by any actions that would undermine Hong Kong's civil liberties and press freedom" and supported the continued development of Hong Kong's democratic institutions.

**16. North Korea Tests an Intercontinental Ballistic Missile**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227165300B5r0elhOc47Mk3Qm.jpg-w600)

The Korean Central News Agency released a photograph claiming the successful test launch of a North Korean-developed intercontinental ballistic missile, the Hwasong-14. The missile flew for 40 minutes and reached a peak altitude of more than 2,500 kilometers; some analysts guessed it could reach Alaska. Because the launch was timed for the eve of the United States' July 4 Independence Day celebrations, it was widely read as a direct challenge to Trump.

**17. KBG48**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173018KCnv0XkYy64lgmux.jpg-w600)

Kohama Island, Japan. Members of KBG48 — the world's oldest idol group, made up entirely of grandmothers — dance in traditional dress. Founded in Okinawa and known in Chinese as the "Kohama Island Grandmother Chorus," the group consists entirely of elderly women and is working toward an appearance on the annual *Kōhaku Uta Gassen* song contest. To join, you must be at least 80; those under 70 are taken on as trainees — on Kohama Island, "eighty is when you really come into your own," and seventy-year-olds may still be finding their feet. The group's 33 members currently average 84 years of age. They have not only released their first album but also completed a domestic concert tour.

**18. Lunar Palace 365**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173050P3ivJ8rsjWcZI0aX.jpg-w600)

Beijing. The second group of volunteers smiles for the camera inside the Lunar Palace 1 space experiment module at Beihang University. In the experiment, named "Lunar Palace 365," they will carry out research and live inside the tightly sealed cabin for 200 days, with food, water, and even oxygen supplied entirely through a self-sustaining closed loop. If it works, it will set a world record for the longest time humans have survived inside a sealed bioregenerative life-support system.

**19. The Iceberg**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173125MWwIj8eXN1GdA7f5.jpg-w600)

Antarctica. A cracked ice shelf. British scientists recently announced that part of the Larsen C Ice Shelf on the Antarctic Peninsula is breaking apart — and the process is speeding up, with full separation from the shelf imminent. The iceberg weighs a trillion tons and is roughly the size of the entire state of Delaware. This alarming development could cause the whole ice shelf to collapse quickly, raising sea levels.

**20. First Anniversary of Turkey's Failed Coup**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227165400dFsB8MXUJEGx2rz3.jpg-w600)

Istanbul, Turkey. People gather on the Bosphorus Bridge for a ceremony marking one year since the failed coup attempt in Turkey. On July 15, 2016, a faction of the Turkish military [tried to overthrow President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/29697.html) and halt the country's Islamization — but the effort collapsed within just two days. Four days after it failed, the Turkish government began a sweeping purge and political vetting of everyone suspected of involvement, across every part of society. By outside estimates, at least 50,000 people nationwide were arrested as a result, while another 150,000 were dismissed or suspended from their jobs.

**21. The Charlottesville Violence**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227165903HT1BdMU90qsXDylV.jpg-w600)

Charlottesville, Virginia, USA. People lay flowers and signs in the street to mourn Heather Heyer, an anti-racism protester killed in the violent clashes. The trigger was the city government's earlier decision to remove a statue of Confederate general Robert E. Lee from the downtown area. White supremacists argued that taking down the statue was an assault on "white American culture and dignity." Opponents countered that the rally had nothing to do with the statue — "they just want to use the rally to spread hatred."

**22. The Barcelona Terror Attack**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227165957PHbhMW5F07RoG8lj.jpg-w600)

Barcelona, Spain. Police escort people evacuated from nearby shops along Las Ramblas, the pedestrian boulevard where the attack happened. On the afternoon of August 17 local time, a white van suddenly sped into the crowd on Las Ramblas, killing at least 13 people and injuring 80, of whom 15 were in serious condition. ISIS [claimed responsibility for the attack](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/44223.html) that same day. Las Ramblas is a famous tree-lined pedestrian boulevard in the city center, 1.2 kilometers long, running from Plaça de Catalunya to the Columbus Monument at the old port. At the time of the attack, Barcelona was at the height of tourist season and the street was packed with visitors. On the evening of August 16 local time, an explosion at a house in Alcanar, about 100 kilometers from Barcelona, had killed one person — police suspect a connection to the attack.

**23. The Philippine Drug War**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227170137eDo5hNWZ3xHPtM8i.jpg-w600)

Manila, Philippines. Philippine police examine the bodies of suspected drug offenders at the scene. Over two consecutive nights of anti-drug operations, at least 57 suspected drug offenders were killed. President Rodrigo Duterte, now 72, had pledged during his campaign to wipe out corruption and the drug trade. According to police figures, at least 3,400 people had been killed in police operations as of July this year.

**24. Looking Straight at It**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173229N3PdSCY69mH25qeX.jpg-w600)

Washington, D.C. President Trump, First Lady Melania, and others watch the total solar eclipse from the White House balcony. Despite repeated warnings from scientists not to look at the sun with the naked eye, Trump still [couldn't resist taking off his glasses](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/44364.html) and staring at the eclipse directly more than once. Some online joked that he did it because he considers scientists' warnings "fake news."

**25. The Rohingya Refugee Crisis**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227170229ASj6ItOX1K7TvaN8.jpg-w600)

Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. A Bangladeshi border officer tells a Rohingya girl she cannot enter the country. Since large-scale armed clashes broke out between Rohingya militants and security forces in Myanmar's Rakhine State in late August, large numbers of Rohingya have crossed the Myanmar-Bangladesh border, trying to reach refugee camps in southern Bangladesh.

**26. Jifeng Bookstore**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228174223LbNFmHxI1OvMQhpa.jpg-w600)

Shanghai. With fewer than 150 days left until the [last Jifeng Bookstore](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/44269.html) (the Shanghai Library branch) closes its doors, passing readers stick farewell postcards bearing personal messages on the walls. The day after [Jifeng announced it would close](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/40059.html) — April 23 — happened to be World Book Day.

**27. Peering Over the Wall**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173321lPrCUaZ1475iLxhT.jpg-w600)

Tecate, USA. A work by French artist JR at the U.S.-Mexico border: a child peering over the dividing wall. On September 5 local time, President Trump announced through Attorney General Jeff Sessions that he was rescinding DACA — the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program signed into law by former president Barack Obama. The order affects 800,000 "Dreamers" — young undocumented immigrants brought to the United States as children by their parents. With DACA rescinded, Dreamers would lose the special protection from deportation they had enjoyed.

**28. Apple's Launch Event**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227170316PvKxF04tINWpRqYX.jpg-w600)

Cupertino, California. Apple CEO Tim Cook shows off the new iPhone X, with Jonathan Ive, head of Apple's design team, beside him. On September 12 local time, Apple [held a launch event](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/45122.html) at the Steve Jobs Theater on its new Apple Park campus and unveiled the iPhone X, iPhone 8, and iPhone 8 Plus, among other products.

**29. Playboy**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173409DObYqPfryWciH1UX.jpg-w600)

(Archival photo) August 21, 1970. *Playboy* magazine founder Hugh Hefner (center left) and French director Roman Polanski (upper left) arrive at Paris Le Bourget Airport aboard Hefner's private jet, Big Bunny. On September 28 local time, *Playboy* announced on its official Twitter account that Hefner had [died](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/45672.html) at home at the age of 91, alongside one of his famous lines: "Life is too short to be living someone else's dream."

**30. The Las Vegas Shooting**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/2017122717041127JpU4HbXPcsiYZj.jpg-w600)

Las Vegas, USA. People climb over fences in search of cover after a [shooting breaks out](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/45817.html) at a country music concert. Just after 10 p.m. local time on October 1, the gunman opened fire from the 32nd floor of the Mandalay Bay Resort and Casino — across the street from the concert — into the crowd below, killing at least 59 people and injuring 527. The suspect, a 64-year-old white man named Stephen Paddock, had a prior criminal record and had checked into the hotel on September 28. He killed himself before police reached the room; officers found 10 rifles inside.

**31. "Comfort Women" Statues**

![Eastern IC](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173612aOeJ8jFLWCUgNIDl.jpg-w600)

Seoul, South Korea. Workers lift a "comfort women" statue onto a vehicle. With the Chuseok holiday approaching, five statues — originally placed in front of the Japanese Embassy — are being readied for a "homecoming journey," traveling with returning holiday traffic to Suwon, Daejeon, Jeonju, Daegu, and Wonju. On September 27, the South Korean National Assembly's Gender Equality and Family Committee passed a bill designating August 14 each year as a day of remembrance for the Japanese military's "comfort women." The bill is expected to clear a plenary session soon; commentators consider it all but certain that the date will become an official day of commemoration starting next year.

**32. The 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China**

![Liu Tong / Eastern IC](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227170603kBCMqbI6T3POJDX7.jpg-w600)

Beijing. Two pedestrians walk along Chang'an Avenue past a three-dimensional themed flower display at the Xidan intersection. The 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China was scheduled for October 18–24. Starting on October 16, Beijing went on full alert. The Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau issued a notice that, from the early hours of the 17th, all aerial photography for sporting, entertainment, or advertising purposes, and all balloon releases, would be banned by any unit, organization, or individual across the city.

**33. Catalonia Declares Independence**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227170655PxtWKrqahE6wyURG.jpg-w600)

Barcelona, Spain. The Catalan parliament votes to pass a resolution declaring independence from Spain in response to the Spanish government's plan to impose direct rule, and pro-independence lawmakers celebrate as they leave. That evening, Spanish Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy gave a televised address declaring Catalan independence illegal and announcing that he had decided to dissolve the Catalan government and remove regional president Carles Puigdemont from office.

**34. Sobbing in Public**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228174824GnK2fu9mMoLW7B8A.jpg-w600)

Nanchang, Jiangxi, November 5. A parent breaks down in tears recounting her child's ordeal during a monthly open day at the Yuzhang Academy (豫章书院). Earlier, several former students who had endured physical punishment and beatings at the school had exposed its dark inner workings on social media. Though the school has had its license revoked, the victims still hope those responsible will be held to account. Notably, the historical Yuzhang Academy was founded in the Southern Song dynasty and closed in 1898; it was once the foremost of Jiangxi's four great academies. Headmaster Wu Junbao opened the present school in 2011, publicly billing it as a "revival" of the academy, saying he wished to "use a return to 'tradition' to awaken improvements in the social climate" and to inspire the post-90s and post-00s generations through classical learning.

**35. The Texas Church Shooting**

![Soobum Im / Eastern IC](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228174727NAIsB0lWg9aoV1LJ.jpg-w600)

Texas, USA. Police cordon off the church in Sutherland Springs where a shooting took place. At midday on the 6th local time, a man walked into the First Baptist Church and opened fire on people who were praying, [killing at least 26, including a pregnant woman and several children](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/46906.html). The suspect was fatally shot as he fled the scene. It was the deadliest mass shooting in the state's history.

**36. Rainbow Marathon**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228173822EdWUBuim41zD6JvF.jpg-w600)

Hangzhou, Zhejiang. The starting gun fires for the 2017 Hangzhou Marathon, and runners in the Rainbow Marathon wave rainbow flags. The annual Hangzhou Rainbow Marathon is organized by the Hangzhou LGBT charity group "Xiangyang Huakai" (Sunflower Blooms) and has been held since 2011. Each year's Rainbow Marathon has a theme; [this year's was "Being Seen."](https://www.douban.com/note/643980360/)

**37. Centenary of the October Revolution**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227170729VIfZSJz8UAXLl4Dy.jpg-w600)

Moscow, Russia. Communist supporters hold portraits of Lenin to mark the 100th anniversary of the October Revolution. The Kremlin's website published a telegram in which Russian President Vladimir Putin welcomed participants in international events commemorating the centenary: "It is entirely natural for social activists, scholars, and media to reflect deeply and fully on this period, expressing a wide range of views and assessments — sometimes diametrically opposed ones. At the same time, I believe that even the fiercest debate should rest on facts and documents, on an objective and respectful attitude toward the past." Asked whether there would be an official commemoration, Putin's spokesperson said: "We have made no plans, and I don't think we have any reason to mark it."

**38. Trump Visits China**

![Andrew Harnik / Eastern IC](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201712271708550df8qKM7uLkJ3ZyI.jpg-w600)

Beijing. President Trump and the First Lady watch three Peking Opera pieces — *Pear Garden Spring Seedlings* (《梨园春苗》), *The Monkey King* (《美猴王》), and *The Drunken Concubine* (《贵妃醉酒》) — and chat with a young performer dressed as the Monkey King. On the afternoon of November 8, Trump arrived in Beijing, beginning his first visit to China since taking office. That evening he posted on Twitter thanking the Chinese side for the grand welcome and saying he looked forward to a full day of meetings with President Xi Jinping and the Chinese delegation. He also changed his Twitter profile background to a photo of himself with Xi Jinping and his wife taken at the Changyin Pavilion. Earlier, during a speech in South Korea, Trump had called on China and other countries to unite in addressing the North Korea issue.

**39. The Victoria's Secret Fashion Show**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228174916rERK1DzA7YVu5nNS.jpg-w600)

Shanghai. At the 2017 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, Chinese model Xi Mengyao takes an accidental tumble on the runway. The show, now in its 23rd year, had drawn criticism for leaning heavily on Western models. This year it broke its own record with 55 models from 20 countries — including eight Chinese models, led by supermodel Liu Wen, also a record number.

**40. Mugabe Resigns**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201712271710241nrYIHbOvM6e8f3G.jpg-w600)

Harare, Zimbabwe. Members of parliament celebrate the resignation of President Robert Mugabe. On the afternoon of November 21 local time, a joint session of Zimbabwe's parliament and senate convened to vote on a motion to impeach Mugabe. As the debate neared its end, the Speaker of the National Assembly, Jacob Mudenda, read out the resignation letter Mugabe had already submitted to lawmakers. Mugabe had led Zimbabwe from 1980 until that point — the first seven years as prime minister and the following 30 as president. His current presidential term had been due to end in August 2018.

**41. The RYB Kindergarten Child Abuse Case**

![Ng Han Guan / Eastern IC](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227171226s6WyZ1NPGrpmLkuQ.jpg-w600)

Beijing. On November 24, parents are still dropping their children off at the RYB New World Kindergarten in Guanzhuang, Chaoyang District. On the evening of November 28, Beijing police released the findings of their investigation into the alleged sexual abuse and mistreatment of children at the RYB New World Kindergarten, confirming that a teacher there had used sewing needles to poke children as a form of "discipline" but finding no evidence of sexual abuse or of children being given unidentified pills. The notice said two parents who had spoken to the media had fabricated their accounts. It added that, while reviewing surveillance footage from the classroom in question, investigators found the storage hard drive had "sustained damage," and the recovered footage "showed no evidence of anyone abusing children."

**42. The Beijing Mass Eviction**

![Li Ke / Eastern IC](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227172511repAWcf146CHwlxo.jpg-w600)

Xinjian Village, Xihongmen Township, Beijing. The most curious people here are probably the children — they likely have no idea what is happening, or why everything is in such disarray. Before the Daxing fire on November 18, Xinjian Village had already been slated for complete demolition as part of the drive to "optimize and upgrade the functions of the capital": not only were the industrial parks housing migrant workers being cleared out, but local residents' farmland was being transferred away too. After the fire, the demolition sped up. Families packed up their belongings and left one low-rise building after another. The great migration that usually comes only before Chinese New Year had arrived early this time.

**43. The Egypt Mosque Attack**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227172359pOZCGQFIh9xL154s.jpg-w600)

Al-Arish, North Sinai Governorate, Egypt. Inside the Sufi mosque that was attacked, blood covers the floor beside a wheelchair. The brutal attack, on November 24 local time, killed at least 305 people — including 27 children — and injured 120 more. It was not only the deadliest attack in Egypt's modern history but also one of the deadliest terrorist attacks anywhere in the world since 9/11. Over the past three years, the Egyptian government has fought militants hard in northern Sinai, at a cost of hundreds of police officers and soldiers killed.

**44. Australia Passes Same-Sex Marriage Legislation**

Canberra, Australia. Members of parliament wave rainbow flags to celebrate the passage of the same-sex marriage bill. **45. Beijing's Skyline**

Beijing. In the name of "restoring a beautiful blue sky over the capital," the rooftop sign of a "national-level technology business incubator" — which had towered over the Zhengyang Bridge on the South Fourth Ring Road since 2003 — has been taken off the city skyline. After releasing the *Beijing Signage and Signboard Management Standards (Revised Edition)* in September, the city's relevant authorities [on November 27](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/47746.html) issued a *Notice on Launching a Special Campaign to Clear the Urban Skyline* and have kept removing exterior-wall and rooftop signs from shopping malls, hotels, residential buildings, and institutions across the city.

**48. The U.S. Passes the Republican Tax Cut Bill**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227172957fxMKrZp9YqJCIl36.jpg-w600)

Washington, D.C. President Trump signs a $1.5 trillion tax reform bill in the Oval Office of the White House — the largest tax cut in the United States in more than 30 years. Bethlehem, West Bank. Palestinians dressed as Santa Claus protest President Trump's recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel. ![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201712281751371e7RTbS4oNInEL3y.jpg-w600)

Tomioka, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. A wild boar roams the empty streets of the nuclear exclusion zone near the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant. To let local residents eventually return home, a team of hunters has been culling wild boar and other radiation-contaminated animals inside the exclusion zone. **51. Reunion**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228175413sCIEDrzXWme5HVRb.jpg-w600)

Algoa Bay, South Africa. Rainer and Silke Schimpf, a couple who work as photographers and marine guides, were out at sea photographing dolphins hunting sardines when they ran into Sira — a disabled orca they had photographed four years earlier. Back then Sira, having lost her dorsal fin and right pectoral fin, could not hunt on her own; it seemed she might be left to fend for herself or even die. The gravely weakened young whale appears to have been cared for by her pod, who shared food with her and let her grow.

**52. Polar Bear**

![@Visual China](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171228175253LY1Pe79XExc3ORhJ.jpg-w600)

Baffin Island, Canada. Photographer Paul Nicklen captures a polar bear — wasted to little more than skin and bone — foraging for food. After he uploaded the image to [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BXyQUA0g_qH/), many followers said they hoped someone could rescue the bear. But Nicklen explained that feeding polar bears is illegal in Canada, and even if the bear could be fed for a while, it would only delay the animal's tragic end a little.

**53. Orangutan Crossing**

![National Geographic](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171227163019G1Rt70u6BnmUFwXD.jpg-w600)

Borneo, Indonesia. A male orangutan is about to cross a river and seems to sense the camera — his expression is distinctly solemn. This photograph, by Singaporean photographer Jayaprakash Joghee Bojan, stood out from 11,000 entries to win this year's National Geographic Nature Photographer of the Year award. In recent years, the relentless spread of palm oil plantations has badly damaged orangutan habitat, and this critically endangered ape faces an ever more desperate situation. To survive, this tree-dwelling species has had to take extraordinary risks — including the perilous crossing of rivers full of crocodiles.
